traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements for Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality: The valid-story-reference rule locates @story annotations, resolves candidate file paths relative to the project root and configured storyDirectories, enforces the .story.md extension (when required), and checks for existence using a cached filesystem layer. Missing files yield fileMissing diagnostics; invalid extensions yield invalidExtension; invalid or out-of-bound paths yield invalidPath. - Quality Standards & Integration: The rule is a proper ESLint RuleModule with meta, schema, and options, uses context.cwd, and integrates cleanly with the overall plugin and configuration system. It operates on annotations already validated by the annotation-format rule, as shown by consistent use of '@story' parsing and extension checks. - User Experience: Error messages (fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, fileAccessError) clearly communicate what is wrong and which path caused the issue, and tests assert both message IDs and data contents. - Error Handling: File system errors (permissions, I/O, arbitrary fs exceptions) are caught, represented as fs-error statuses, and surfaced as fileAccessError diagnostics instead of causing crashes. This is thoroughly covered by dedicated Jest tests. - Security & Project Boundary: Absolute paths are rejected by default; traversal outside the project is blocked via path resolution and enforceProjectBoundary; misconfigured storyDirectories pointing outside the project cannot cause external files to be treated as valid. All of these behaviors are explicitly tested under REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION and REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - Performance Optimization: Existence checks are cached in a Map keyed by absolute path, minimizing repeat fs operations during a lint run. There is a dedicated cache reset helper for tests, and the implementation never disables caching in production. While the story’s DoD notes performance testing as a separate checkbox (which remains unchecked in the doc), the required behavior (efficient, cached filesystem access) is implemented. - Configurability: storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, and requireStoryExtension options are implemented with schema validation and tested in multiple scenarios, satisfying REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS.
Given the passing targeted tests and the alignment of implementation and documentation with all specified requirements, this story is fully implemented and passes.
